title: Reverse Bits
summary: Reverse the binary representation of a 32-bit signed integer.
statement: Reverse the binary representation of a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: The retained source contract specifies an EVEN integer n with 0 ≤ n ≤ 2^31 - 2.
Reverse all 32 bit positions, including leading zeroes, and return the resulting integer. Do not reverse only the nonzero-width binary representation.
target_time_complexity: O(32), constant for the fixed width
hints: The width is fixed even when the input number needs only a few nonzero bit positions.
Read the input from its least-significant bit while shifting the output left.
Repeat exactly 32 times: append n&1 to the output, then shift n right by one.
For n=2, the single set bit at position 1 moves to position 30, giving 1073741824.
editorial: Each iteration removes one low input bit and appends it to the high-to-low construction of the answer. Exactly 32 iterations preserve leading zero positions. The independent oracle formats a 32-character binary string and reverses that string. Tests follow the retained upstream even, nonnegative signed-range constraint rather than importing historical unsigned examples outside this source snapshot. Under that constraint the returned number also fits a nonnegative signed-32-bit value.

tests.explanation: The two low zero bits become two high zero bits. Reversing the full 32-bit pattern gives 1073741822.
